cases.oracle: Registry: stone (type 3) and wood (type 4) carry hardness 3 while grass (type 1) and dirt (type 2) carry hardness 1. With a fresh default world (terrain rows y<4 grass, y<10 dirt, y<18 stone, else wood), the first hit on the stone at cell (5,12) leaves the block present, records per-cell damage hits=1 and produces crack overlay stage 1 as a pure function of (x, y, stage) with no assets; the second hit leaves it present with hits=2 and crack stage 2 distinct from stage 1; pointermove inside the same cell adds no hits (damage accrues on cell-entry edges only); the third hit reaches hardness 3, removes the block (cell becomes 0), clears its damage-map entry and increments the stone (type 3) inventory by exactly 1; wood at (5,18) behaves identically (3 hits to remove, +1 wood inventory, same crack staging).

With a fresh default world, a single click on the grass at cell (10,2) removes it immediately (cell becomes 0), increments the grass (type 1) inventory by exactly 1, and leaves no damage-map entry and no crack overlay for that cell; dirt at cell (10,5) likewise is removed on the first hit (hardness 1) with +1 dirt (type 2) inventory.

Selecting a type from the palette and placing into an empty cell requires that type inventory > 0 and decrements it by exactly 1 while the cell takes the placed type; with that type inventory exactly 0 a placement attempt is refused before any mutation (the cell stays empty, the count stays 0, and the palette entry for that type renders greyed out at zero); inventory remains non-negative integers over types 1..4 and never goes negative.

After a mine-then-place sequence changing both world and inventory, the save written at the single key minicraft-grid-v1 is one atomic blob {version:2, cells, inventory} with cells of length 400 (values 0..4) and inventory of non-negative integers over keys 1..4; a reload (fresh boot reading the same key) restores world cells and inventory deep-equal to the pre-reload state while the transient damage map resets to empty; a stored v1 blob {version:1, cells} migrates on load with inventory defaulted to 0 for every type; with empty localStorage the first boot yields the default terrain world and an all-zero inventory.

cleanup.environment: Run from the repo root with the Node >= 18 built-in test runner; no browser, dev server or network access required; the run must leave no environment mutation.
cleanup.data: The logic suite injects an in-memory storage stub for the save key; no real browser localStorage, world blob or project file is written, and a completed run leaves no data artifacts.
